## Goal

As a player, I want the closing screen to distinguish the voyage I actually made — including quitting early — so that the epilogue score means something.

Found during the spike observation log (`docs/gym/long-erasure-observation-log.md`, §4.4 / §2, `CG-0MWNHZEGJ0099JFM`): the epilogue grants the **full arc award (60 points) for entering any ending card**, including the deliberately terminal `Abandon the voyage` reached in Act II.

Measured (named routes, `npx tsx scripts/long-erasure-playtest.ts`):

- `abandon` (5 choices, 6 beats, ~80 words of prose, 9 clock left): score **79** — arc 60 + choices 10 + resources 13 − losses 4 → band "A voyage that left a mark", 4 points below finishing.
- `reset-cheap` (7 choices, 8 beats, ~106 words, 4 clock left): score **83** — arc 60 + choices 12 + resources 15 − losses 4 → top band.
- 56 of 160 policy runs took the abandon hatch; every one lands in (or immediately below) the top band.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Abandoning the voyage in Act II can no longer score in the top band: the arc component must reflect the acts *played*, not the ending card entered (e.g. arc credit only for acts advanced beyond, and a reduced/zero arc award for an `abandon` outcome).
- A finishing route still outscores the abandon terminal by a clear margin (>= 15 points), asserted by a unit test on `scoreRun` / `buildEpilogue` in `tests/gym/`.
- The band labels and the documented score table in `GymLongErasureGame.ts` stay consistent with the new rule, and the scene help text's epilogue description still holds.
- `npx tsx scripts/long-erasure-playtest.ts --seeds 40 --route "abandon=…"` reports the abandon route in a band below the finishing routes.

## Key Files

- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` (`JOURNEY_SCORE_TABLE`, `scoreRun`, `enterCard` act bookkeeping)
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureGame.test.ts`, `tests/gym/LongErasureEpilogue.test.ts`
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts` (help text)
- `scripts/long-erasure-playtest.ts` (verification harness)
- `docs/gym/long-erasure-observation-log.md` (§4.4 / §7)

## Notes

Discovered from `CG-0MWNHZEGJ0099JFM` (observation log). This is the measured evidence behind the GDD question "must endings be distinguishable?" (`CG-0MWNFVLYT003M7XF`); fixing it here keeps the Gym spike honest as a demonstrator, and the same rule should inform the full game's epilogue.
data.title: Gym Long Erasure: epilogue must not award full arc credit for abandoning the voyage

data.description:
## Goal

Make the epilogue's arc component reflect the acts a run actually played, so abandoning the voyage cannot
collect the Act III award — the implementation half of parent `CG-0MWNSR376002QBY9`.

Root cause (measured): `enterCard` credits every act up to the `Ending` rank on entering *any* ending card
(`recordActsBefore(working, ACT_RANK.Ending)`), so `Abandon the voyage` — entered from Act II at
`le-ii-offer` — collects the full 60 arc points. The fix credits the acts played through: a run that ends
credits the act it was in when it ended, so an abandon from Act II credits Acts I–II (35) while a finishing
run from Act III still credits Acts I–III (60).

Predicted authoring-content outcomes with the rule: abandon 54 ("A voyage the erasure nearly kept", two bands
below the top), reset-cheap 83 (top band, unchanged), expiry unchanged (no credit for the unplayed beat).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `enterCard` no longer credits arc for the `Ending` rank itself: a run that reaches an ending credits exactly the acts it played through (the act the ending beat was entered from), so the authored abandon credits `['I', 'II']` (arc 35) and every finishing ending credits `['I', 'II', 'III']` (arc 60).
- The rule is content-agnostic: `GymLongErasureGame.ts` contains no reference to the abandon ending's id (`le-end-abandon`) or its label; crediting derives only from `ACT_RANK` and the run's current act, so any future ending reached from Act II inherits the rule.
- The no-successor terminal close path in `chooseOption` applies the same rule (both close paths agree), proven by a unit test over a minimal hand-built `LongErasureContent` fixture whose terminal option pushes no card.
- Act gating (`'backward-act'`), clock expiry (`outcome: 'expired'`, which credits nothing for the unplayed beat), reset detection (`outcome: 'reset'`) and the `[0, 100]` clamp are unchanged, and the existing module + epilogue suites pass without edits to their expectations.
- The `JOURNEY_SCORE_TABLE` docblock states the new `arc` rule and keeps the "authored content tops out at 92 (60 + 12 + 20)" sentence true; no weight, cap, band threshold or band label changes.
- The sibling test item's regression cases go from red to green, and the changed-scope unit suite (`/skill:test --type unit`) plus `npm run build` pass before the commit.

**Key Files:**

- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` (`enterCard`, `recordActsBefore`, `chooseOption`, `JOURNEY_SCORE_TABLE`)
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureEpilogue.test.ts`
- `tests/gym/GymLongErasureGame.test.ts`

**Covers parent AC:** "the arc component must reflect the acts *played*, not the ending card entered".
data.title: Long Erasure: credit only played acts when a run ends

## Summary

Write the GDD's tension, pacing, failure and reset-ending scoring design: the clock as a visible per-scene budget, irreversible loss as the tension dial, numeric pacing rules, failure and recovery for each failure type, and a precise scoring model justified against the "earned, not punitive" test.

## Target outcome

A designer can judge whether the ending feels earned rather than punitive, because the scoring inputs, weights and band table are written down and traceable to what the player did.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Tension design is specified with the clock as a visible per-scene budget and at least one recovery path; no clock outcome may silently delete content from the run.
- Irreversible loss is specified as a concrete mechanism, with its cost, its benefit and its interaction with the scene budget.
- Pacing rules are stated numerically: beats per scene, decisions per scene, minimum rejoin distance for consequential choices, and act-length targets.
- Failure and recovery are specified per failure type (scene failure, budget exhaustion, resource at zero), stating what the player keeps and how the run continues.
- The reset-ending scoring model is defined precisely: inputs, weights or rubric, band table, and the exact summary the player sees.
- The scoring model is justified against the "earned, not punitive" test, including why abandoning early cannot land in the top band.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write a tension section with one measured example per rule.
- Write the scoring model as an inputs table plus a worked score for a recorded run.
- Write a failure/recovery table per failure type.
- Reconcile the model with the open epilogue finding (`CG-0MWNSR376002QBY9`).

## Risky assumptions

- The scoring formula is untested; the section must show one worked score per band so a reviewer can check the arithmetic.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the playtest evaluation, the GDD foundation and the resource model.

## Key Files

- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — the tension, pacing, failure and scoring sections.
- `docs/gym/long-erasure-observation-log.md` — the measured clock and score findings.
- `example-games/gym/GymLongErasureGame.ts` — the current journal-derived score to build on.
- `tests/gym/LongErasureEpilogue.test.ts` — the existing epilogue expectations.

## Impact

A reviewer can check that the ending is earned by reading the formula rather than by trusting the design intent.
data.title: GDD tension, pacing, failure and reset-ending scoring

## Summary

Write the GDD's presentation and technical contract: SLL zone names for every surface, overlay and HUD behaviour, audio/SFX mapping, accessibility, and determinism, save/load, transcript and replay expectations.

## Target outcome

An implementer knows which SLL zones and HUD components to use and which events must be animated and sounded, so the game is consistent with every other TCE game on day one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- UI surfaces are specified with SLL zone names for each surface (resource HUD, act/scene banner, objective panel, choice list, journal, epilogue screen), with no absolute pixel coordinates.
- Overlay behaviour is specified for help, settings, journal and confirmation, following the project's depth-ordered overlay convention.
- Audio and SFX mapping is specified with `COMMON_SFX_KEYS` names per event, plus the reduced-motion alternative for each animated event.
- Accessibility is specified: reduced motion, verbosity and tooltips, colour-independent signalling, and keyboard and touch input paths.
- Determinism, save/load, transcript and replay expectations are stated: seeded RNG, serialisation version, transcript event set and replay determinism.
- Every surface or capability named is either already available in the engine or listed in the engine-gap backlog.

## Minimal Implementation

- Write one table per concern with the engine API or zone name in the right-hand column.
- Cite the existing Gym scene that demonstrates each pattern.
- Mark every unavailable capability as a backlog pointer, not a promise.

## Risky assumptions

- The GDD proposes surfaces that do not exist yet (act/scene transition presentation). Each must be explicit as a gap.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the GDD foundation and the resource model.

## Key Files

- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — the presentation and technical sections.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — SLL, HUD, audio and replay references to cite.
- `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` — the SFX key convention.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymLongErasureScene.ts` — the spike's rendered surface.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymOverlayUiScene.ts` — the overlay and clipping reference.

## Impact

An implementer can build the game's presentation by zone name and SFX key instead of inventing a layout and an audio map.
data.title: GDD presentation contract: UI, audio, accessibility, determinism

## Summary

Close the writer-facing authoring frictions measured by the Long Erasure spike, so a writer can add a branch to an existing story-line without retyping whole cells, guessing an authoring order, or dropping into the editor for prose.

Discovered-from: CG-0MWPY29730011FJ4 (GDD writer content pipeline, which documents each friction as a known limit and points here).

## The frictions (all re-verified at the GDD commit)

1. **Forward references are refused.** `storylines:author update-card` rejects an option naming a card that does not exist yet (`links to unknown card "gx-ghost"`), so a branch must be authored backwards from its target. `add-card` alone on an existing story-line can also flip the entry card and report every other card as `unreachable-card`.
2. **`update-card --options` replaces the whole cell.** Adding one option means retyping every existing option; a dropped `;` silently removes a branch until validation catches it.
3. **Every row repeats the full declared resource set.** The `resources` column is per-card, so the same key list is copied into every row; a mismatch is only caught downstream.
4. **No positional insert.** `add-card` appends, so CSV reading order drifts from narrative order.
5. **The author CLI cannot author prose.** `--field context=...` is refused ("field \"context\" is a mapped story-line column"), and the CLI has no `--context` / `--epilogue` flag, so prose can be authored only through the editor or its `--apply` bridge.

Mitigations that already exist (and must not regress): the editor's `add-linked-card` edit adds the card **and** the predecessor option in one validated transaction; stale content is refused; every diagnostic carries row, column and reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An option can be appended to an existing card without retyping the cell (an `add-option` author operation, or `add-linked-card` parity in the CLI).
- A writer can supply `--context` and `--epilogue` through `storylines:author` (`add-card` and `update-card`), or an equivalent documented path with no editor session.
- The resource key set is declared once per content file (or defaulted from a predecessor) instead of repeated per row, with the declared set still validated per card.
- `add-card` can insert at a documented position (append, or after a named card), and appending to an existing multi-member story-line cannot silently re-point the entry card.
- Forward-reference authoring has a documented, single-transaction path (author the option and its target together), so a branch is never half-authored.
- Each change is covered by unit tests over the author/edit seams, and the GDD's `§2.9` friction table is updated to "resolved" with the command that resolves it.
- `npm run build` and the unit profile are green.

## Key Files

- `scripts/storyline-author.ts` — CLI flags and subcommands.
- `src/story-line/content/mutate.ts` — `addContentCard`, `updateContentCard`, spec shapes (already carry `context` / `epilogue`).
- `src/story-line/editor/edits.ts` — `add-linked-card` (the existing single-transaction precedent).
- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` — per-file resource declaration seam.
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md`, `docs/dev/storyline-editor.md` — authoring docs.
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` §2.9 — the friction table this item closes out.

## Impact

A writer can add, edit and prose a story branch from the command line in one validated step instead of retyping whole cells or switching tools.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MWNHZ7DA00243HB** – Writer-authorable CSV option fields (completed)
- **CG-0MVHZ2KE40011Z0S** – Storyline content and authoring toolchain generalised into core (completed)
- **CG-0MWO7EOJQ001090X** – Close coverage gap: A beat can author a `context` paragraph, per-option outcome prose and an ending epilogue **entire... (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: acceptance, adapters, add, adding, adds (+168 more)
- `docs/core-engine/story-line.md` — matched: adapters, add, addcontentcard, adds, alone (+141 more)
- `docs/design/storyline-game-gdd.md` — matched: 0mwpy29730011fj4, acceptance, add, adding, adds (+137 more)

## Summary
Declare the resource key set once per content file instead of repeating it on every row, while still validating each card against the declared set.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A content CSV may open with a `#resources: hull,morale,stores,goodwill,charge` comment line (or equivalent adapter-level declaration), which becomes the file's default declared set
- A card row that leaves `resources` blank inherits the file's declared set
- A card row that sets `resources` explicitly overrides the file default (for mixed-resource files)
- `unknown-resource-key` still fires when an option references a key outside the effective declared set for the card
- Existing content files with per-row `resources` cells continue to validate unchanged (backward compatible)
- `npm test -- --project unit` and `npm run build` are green

- `src/story-line/content/csv.ts` — `parseCsv` (extract leading comment/declaration lines), `cardsFromCsv`
- `src/story-line/content/adapters.ts` — optional `defaultResources` on `ContentAdapter` / `ContentFileSpec`
- `src/story-line/content/validate.ts` — resource declaration resolution before `unknown-resource-key`
